mutants.description: Cournot volume taken as the monopoly volume d/2 while the Cournot fee keeps its own formula.
Input check accepts a zero unit cost (c < 0 instead of c <= 0), so c = 0 is not rejected.
Deadweight loss computed from the rounded volume half_up(volume) instead of the exact volume, which the spec forbids.
Cournot volume_trades reports one exchange's quantity d/3 instead of the two-exchange total 2d/3.
An unknown structure name raises KeyError from a dict lookup, not the ValueError the page names.
Cournot exchange profit is doubled: the margin times the volume is counted once per exchange and then again.
Monopoly profit is taken on the gap d instead of the monopoly volume d/2, so profit is (fee - c) times d.
Cournot fee is computed from the printed trade volume, (a - round(volume))/b, not from the exact volume.
Cournot volume from 61 steps of the best-response iteration in exact fractions, not the closed form 2d/3.
Bertrand fee is the gap per unit of b, d/b, instead of the cost c, so the fee is not the marginal cost.
Gross value is (a Q - Q^2)/b instead of (a Q - Q^2/2)/b, so welfare is wrong by Q^2/(2b) in every structure.
Deadweight loss is (d - Q)^2/b, with the factor 2 of the triangle dropped from the denominator.
Cournot profit rounds each exchange's margin separately and doubles the result, not one rounding of the exact total.
Volume is rounded up to the next whole trade (a ceiling), not to the nearest trade with a tie going up.
Rounding by Python round(), which sends an exact half to the even neighbour, so a tie does not go up.
Deadweight loss measured from the printed volume half_up(volume), not the exact volume.
The first input check is strict, so a equal to b*c is accepted instead of raising ValueError.
The structure name is lowercased before the check, so the capitalised name Monopoly is accepted.
Consumer surplus taken as the fee times the volume, the exchange revenue, not the area above the fee.

Invalid inputs return six zero outputs instead of raising ValueError, a silent fallback.
Trade volume rounded by Python round(), so an exact half trade goes to the even neighbour; money keys still go up.

Bertrand volume is the gap divided by b, not the gap, so the volume is wrong for every b above 1.
